_comment: Declared, reasoned differences between NXD's production semantic MCP surface
and the eval harness's server. Every entry is a place a scenario cannot see a
production regression, so each one needs a reason a reader can act on.
An UNDECLARED difference fails the semantic-contract job. So does an entry that
no longer describes a real difference, which keeps this file from rotting into
Descriptions are not compared here: the eval server paraphrases them for its
own scenarios. NXD's producer-side contract tests pin the descriptions against
the factory and extracted entrypoints that actually serve them.

missing_tools.name: semantic_model
missing_tools.reason: The eval server serves the agent-facing catalog through list_models and describe_model, which is what the graded scenarios drive. semantic_model returns the FULL registry as one JSON payload and exists for cross-DP planning; no eval scenario plans across meshes through the tool surface, so adding it would be untested substrate. Revisit when a scenario grades cross-DP discovery through the tools rather than through fixtures.

missing_parameters.reason: The eval server compiles selections directly through compile_selection with no ordering. Top-N behaviour is exercised by NXD's own compiler tests; wiring order_by here would add an eval-side code path with no scenario grading it.
Same as order_by: the governed executor already applies its own row cap, so a caller-supplied limit would change what the executor's cap means without any scenario measuring the difference.

parameter_mismatches.reason: Production's RPC-to-pydantic conversion leaves an undescribed nullable field out of the JSON Schema's required set, so name reads as optional over the wire even though describe_model cannot answer without it. The eval server types it as a plain str, hence required. The eval side is the stricter of the two and is the behaviour scenarios should grade; this entry records that the laxer production schema is known and deliberate.

Same conversion detail as describe_model.name: measures carries a description, and the converter marks a described nullable field optional. Production's own tool description states measures is REQUIRED, and the compiler refuses a selection without it, so the eval server's required-by-signature form matches the real contract more closely than the generated schema does.
